description: Sparse MLA attention: each token attends to the KV-pool slots its top-k indices name (-1 skipped); scores q . kv * sm_scale with q = [q_nope, q_rope], values the first d_v features. sglang triton_sparse_mla_fwd / flash_mla_sparse / aiter sparse MLA, decode and prefill (DSA models).

context.doc: resident tokens the indices are drawn from

pool.doc: KV pool slots allocated in the case

call: Invoke the live entry with the backend's keyword names (q_nope, q_rope, kv, indices, sm_scale, d_v) and return (output, lse). If the deployment passes a strided q (q_nope/q_rope as views of one buffer), build that layout in a case of its own.

timing.cache: kv is the long-lived pool; at long context the gathered rows are cold. indices are stratified across the whole context (sparse_indices) because the selector picks from a context far longer than topk; a contiguous window would be L2-friendly and too fast.

negative_controls: drop the rope part of the score (q_nope . kv[:d_v] only): every probability changes
treat index -1 as slot 0 instead of skipping it: rows with padding attend to a stray value
pitfalls: The decode branch runs inside the CUDA graph: hooks fired during graph capture see placeholder buffers, so an oracle captured there is all zeros and 'passes' with max_rel_err 0.0. Seeded inputs avoid capture entirely; if one is ever used, take it from an eager leg.
Split-K over the top-k gather is chosen by batch size: replay sigs must span the kv_splits ladder (smallest served batch, modal batch, largest batch, largest captured graph size).
Rows with no valid index return output 0 and lse -inf in sglang's triton kernel; FlashMLA's sparse API returns +inf. Match the entry under test.
Allocate the pool once per case at the size the case needs: a pool sized for the largest case makes every small decode case gather from a cold, sparse region it would not touch when served.
